aura-guard.tagline: Gradient‑boosting forecasts improve on persistence by up to 30 % at the six‑hour horizon.
aura-guard.plain: The app delivers short‑term NO₂ forecasts for US monitors and a question‑answering agent that only returns numbers that can be traced to those forecasts.
aura-guard.summary: AURA‑GUARD combines a React front‑end with a Node API and a Python gradient‑boosting model trained on EPA hourly NO₂ data from twenty US monitors. The model is back‑tested with walk‑forward validation, achieving a 30 % MAE reduction over persistence at six‑hour ahead forecasts. The repository contains 99 source files, a CI workflow, nine test files and an LLM‑driven analyst that is constrained by a deterministic checker to ensure every numeric claim is grounded in the model output.
aura-guard.highlight: The difficult part was building a deterministic grounding checker that forces the LLM to cite only model‑derived values and to reject or correct answers about missing monitors, preventing untraceable or false statements.

finverse.tagline: Finverse combines a micro‑service stack with JWT‑based permission checks to protect personal finance data.
finverse.plain: It is a personal finance assistant that stores transactions and offers AI‑driven advice.
finverse.summary: The repository contains a four‑service JavaScript and Python codebase organised into frontend, backend, AI engine and data directories. The frontend uses React with TypeScript, the backend runs Node.js with Express and SQLite via Sequelize, and the AI engine is a Flask service that calls Google Gemini. A Redis instance is used for rate limiting and session handling. The project includes twelve test files and a linter configuration but no CI workflow or deployment scripts.
finverse.highlight: Ensuring that JWT authentication integrates with a granular permission system while also supporting rate‑limiting required careful coordination between the Express API, Redis and the AI Flask service.

gtu-ai-attendance-system.tagline: The system combines a Python AI service with a Next.js frontend to optimise student attendance schedules.
gtu-ai-attendance-system.plain: It helps students plan attendance by analysing timetables and preferences using AI.
gtu-ai-attendance-system.summary: The repository contains a Next.js 15.5.3 frontend, an Express.js backend, and a Flask AI service that calls Gemini 1.5 Flash. The codebase includes Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, CSS and shell scripts, with a package.json manifest and several test files. Documentation is provided in a README and deployment guides, but no licence or deployment is configured.
gtu-ai-attendance-system.highlight: Integrating Gemini AI responses with attendance optimisation required handling asynchronous AI calls while maintaining consistent schedule calculations.

hashhawks.tagline: The code blends Spline 3D graphics with a type‑safe React UI in a Vite build.
hashhawks.plain: A web site that shows interactive 3D visuals and scrolling effects using modern JavaScript tools.
hashhawks.summary: The repository contains a Vite‑powered React application written in TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui components. It includes 69 source files across 56 component modules, a Tailwind configuration, PostCSS setup and a Spline‑driven 3D visual layer. The project provides scripts for development, production build and preview, but no test suite or CI configuration is present.
hashhawks.highlight: Integrating real‑time Spline 3D graphics into a React component tree while preserving fast Vite builds and responsive Tailwind layouts required careful synchronisation of animation frames and type‑safe props.

voice-emotion-detection.tagline: Closing hidden leaks raises the honest macro‑F1 to 0.77 for a frozen WavLM model.
voice-emotion-detection.plain: The code evaluates speech emotion recognition on RAVDESS while preventing speaker‑dependent bias.
voice-emotion-detection.summary: The repository contains Python source, Jupyter notebooks and scripts for training and evaluating speech emotion classifiers on the RAVDESS dataset. It includes a frozen WavLM model with a linear classifier that achieves a macro‑F1 of 0.77 on eight emotions under a speaker‑independent cross‑validation protocol. Tests verify the leakage fixes and the evaluation pipeline, and continuous‑integration workflows run the test suite. Documentation comprises a detailed README, a model card and result visualisations.
voice-emotion-detection.highlight: Identifying and closing three subtle data‑leakage paths in the original RAVDESS pipeline required redesigning the split, augmentation handling and validation to ensure the model never sees a speaker’s voice during training.
